_doc: BRIEF SCHEMA v2 — three-tier model. The v1 schema captured WHAT a campaign is about (subject/occasion/headline) but NOT how the scene is constructed (staging/props/composition/text-layout). The 9-vs-7 quality gap lives entirely in that missing 'how' layer. v2 adds it as a tier the SYSTEM fills for the human, because a non-designer cannot author it. Target user: marketing manager, not pro designer. Core principle unchanged: no field governed by two owners.
_quality_finding: Proven on Taichi garden-tomato poster (June 2026): a hand-authored brief with full scene-construction detail (gradient hex stops, hero staging, 4 prop placements, 6 text layers, camera angle) produced a 9/10 vs target. The same pipeline with only the v1 4-slot brief produces ~7. The variance is the scene layer. Also proven: a reference image carries product-silhouette + type quality that text cannot name — so the reference is a first-class slot, not optional decoration.

lock_levels.hard_lock: Brand value is final. Brief CANNOT override. If brief tries, refuse + keep brand value.
lock_levels.default_strong: Brand value is the default. Brief may NUDGE within range (bounded), not replace.
lock_levels.default_weak: Brand value is a default. Brief freely overrides.
lock_levels.system_authored: NEW. Neither brand nor human authors this directly. The system constructs it from (intent + reference + occasion), then shows it to the human for approval. This is the scene-construction layer — the thing a non-designer cannot write but can react to.

tier_1_identity._desc: Who the brand is. Locked or nudge-only. Comes from the VI analysis layer.

tier_2_intent._owner: HUMAN (brief_owned) — the ONLY tier the manager authors directly
tier_2_intent._desc: What the campaign is about. The manager CAN answer these in one sentence each. This is the v1 brief, kept as-is.

subject.ask: What is the material for / what should it show? (e.g. 'new spicy chicken burger')

headline_message.ask: What's the main message or headline text?

feeling.ask: In a few words, what feeling should it give? (e.g. 'fresh, garden, premium')
feeling._note: drives the system's tier-3 palette/staging choices when off-VI

reference_image.ask: Got an image whose look you like, or a photo of the actual product? Drop it in.
reference_image._note: FIRST-CLASS slot. Carries product silhouette + type quality text cannot name. Tagged by role: identity / style_exemplar / product_form.

tier_3_scene_construction._owner: SYSTEM (system_authored) — the bottleneck layer, built FOR the human
tier_3_scene_construction._desc: How the scene is physically built. This is what separated the 9 from the 7. The manager cannot author these; the system proposes them from (tier_2 intent + reference + occasion), renders them as a plain-language preview, and the human approves or nudges. THIS is the elicitation layer's real job.

palette_resolved._desc: If on-VI: brand colors. If off-VI campaign (occasion+feeling imply it): system proposes a campaign palette WITH gradient stops, flags it as a departure, asks human to confirm. Taichi teal #7BA89F->#6B9B92->cream came from here.

background._desc: Backdrop + gradient direction + surface. e.g. 'muted teal top fading to cream beige staged surface bottom 20%'.

hero_staging._desc: How the subject is presented: elevation, surface/prop it sits on, angle, lighting, depth of field. e.g. 'elevated on light-oak pedestal w/ draped linen, 3/4 angle ~15deg, soft diffused, shallow DoF'. When a product-form reference exists, this defers to it for silhouette.

props._desc: Supporting scene elements w/ rough placement. e.g. 'woven tomato basket lower-left, scattered basil, white salsa bowl lower-right'. Derived from subject+feeling.

text_layout._desc: Each text element: content + position + color + rough scale. The 9 had 6 of these. System maps headline_message + brand_name + occasion copy into positioned layers.

composition._desc: Negative space, focal hierarchy, balance. default_weak from brand, refined by system.

tier_3_scene_construction._human_loop: System fills all tier-3 fields, then renders ONE plain-language summary ('A wide poster: fresh teal background fading to cream, your burger raised on a light-wood stand with a cream cloth, tomatoes in a basket to the left, basil scattered, your headline big in white down both sides...'). Human reads it like a sentence, says 'yes' or 'make the background warmer' / 'no basket'. Nudges re-run only the touched field. The human never writes the slot — they react to it.

elicitation_flow._desc: How a non-designer reaches a 9-quality brief. Three steps, escalating system involvement.
elicitation_flow.step_1_intent: Ask only the tier-2 questions (4 hard + feeling + optional reference). One sentence each. This is all the human authors.
elicitation_flow.step_2_construct: System reads tier-1 (brand) + tier-2 (intent) + reference, decides on-VI vs off-VI, and AUTHORS all of tier-3. This is the model doing what a designer's brain does — decomposing intent into a buildable scene.
elicitation_flow.step_3_approve: Show the tier-3 plan as plain language (not JSON). Human approves or nudges in plain language. Loop until 'yes'. Then assemble the final prompt + reference and generate.
elicitation_flow._win_condition: FALSIFIABLE TEST: a naive user runs steps 1-3 and lands a >=8 against a known target, WITHOUT a designer in the loop. If the system's tier-3 authoring reproduces the hand-built scene quality, the prompt specificity is no longer 'out of the human's hands'. That is the proof the whole project hinges on.

guardrails.completeness: If any tier-2 hard slot empty -> ASK (one targeted question). Never guess intent.
guardrails.identity: If brief attempts to set a tier-1 hard_lock field -> REFUSE, keep brand value, tell the user it's brand-locked.
guardrails.off_vi_consent: If system proposes an off-VI palette (tier-3 palette_resolved departs from brand colors), it MUST flag the departure and get explicit human confirmation. Never silently abandon brand colors.
guardrails.scene_not_authored_by_human: Tier-3 is system_authored. Do NOT ask the human to write staging/props/text-layout. Ask intent; construct scene; show for approval. Asking a non-designer to author tier-3 recreates the exact bottleneck this schema exists to remove.
